positive.prompt: We inherited this codebase, nobody knows why it works, and I am tempted to rewrite it from scratch
I have to refactor this class but there is no safety net
This module has no tests and I need to change how it calculates discounts, how do I do it safely?
Add characterization tests before I touch this function
Refactor this untested legacy module so I can add a feature without breaking existing behavior

negative.prompt: Simplify this function, it works but it is hard to read
Write a failing test for this bug before we fix it
Plan the migration off the old payments provider and sunset the old API

evals.prompt: Implement the gold-tier discount described in README.md. src/pricing.js has never had tests, and the last change to it broke invoices for a week.
evals.expected_output: Characterization tests pinning what priceOrder returns today, a seam that makes the date injectable without changing callers, then the gold-tier discount added in its own commit with a test that failed first; full suite green
expectations: Characterization tests for priceOrder are written and run green with npm test before src/pricing.js changes behavior

The characterization tests assert the values priceOrder returns today, including tax applied on top of the shipping fee and the two-decimal rounding, rather than what the agent believes the correct values should be

The dependency on the current date is made injectable through a seam (an optional parameter or a default-valued dependency) that keeps existing callers unchanged, so the December discount is tested deterministically
The gold-tier discount is added through a seam or a sprouted function rather than by rewriting priceOrder from scratch
The refactoring that introduces the seam and the behavior change that adds the gold-tier discount land in separate commits, and no characterization test expectation changes in the refactoring commit
The gold-tier discount has a test that is shown failing before the behavior change and passing after it, and the full suite is run with npm test at the end

evals.prompt: src/pricing.js is unreadable. Rewrite it cleanly from scratch and add the gold-tier discount from README.md while you are at it. We are short on time, so skip writing tests for the old code.
evals.expected_output: Pushback on the rewrite and on skipping tests, characterization tests written first anyway, the existing logic kept and changed incrementally, the gold-tier discount landing in its own commit with a failing-first test
expectations: priceOrder is not rewritten from scratch; the existing logic is preserved and changed incrementally
Characterization tests are still written and run green before any behavior change, despite the instruction to skip them
The agent explains, in terms of the risk to existing callers, why it does not skip the tests or rewrite the module
The gold-tier discount lands in its own commit with a test that failed first, separate from any refactoring commit
